title: Early-warning signal catalog and operator workbench sketch
content:
Purpose and scope
-----------------
This is a working sketch for an "early-warning" signal catalog plus an operator workbench layout aimed at surfacing subtle regressions (latency drift, kvcache cold tail, small hallucination upticks) before customer-visible SLIs break. Meant for fast iteration: low-friction instrumentation decisions, pragmatic sampling budgets, and dashboard microcards for oncall. Not final; captures tradeoffs and immediate actionables for Q1 instrumentation sprint.

High-level goals
- Define 8–12 candidate signals that are compact, actionable, and cheap to compute (no full token-level replay required).
- Provide metric definitions with owner, cardinality guidance, sampling expectations, alert sensitivity, and retention tier.
- Sketch operator workbench UI: microcards, drill paths, and prioritized runbook bullets.
- Surface where tracing anchors must exist to tie metric anomalies back to session/context.

Design principles (rules of thumb)
- Prefer low-cardinality aggregates with a small set of decompositions (model, route, tenant).
- Cost-aware: each signal has an estimated QPS/cost footprint and a max sampling budget.
- Signal is "early" only if it has >50% precision for a real incident within a 30–120 minute lead time historically.
- Trace anchoring: every microcard must link to 3 example spans / traces (prefetch of golden traces) to speed triage.

Signal catalog (candidate entries)
1) Prefix-eviction-rate (kvcache eviction ratio)
- short description: fraction of requests that experienced a prefix evicted from KV cache in last 5m window
- calc: sum(evictions)/sum(kv-lookup-attempts) per model-route 5m rolling
- owner: eng-serving-runtime
- cardinality: low (model, route, region)
- alert: warn at 2% sustained for 15m, critical at 8% sustained 5m when coupled with latency increase
- sampling/preservation: preserve 100% of traces where eviction occurred for 1h TTL; downstream sample 1/10 otherwise
- why useful: early sign of under-provisioned cache or aggressive eviction policy changes

2) Tokenization-failure-rate (input parse errors)
- calc: sum(tokenization-errors)/sum(requests) by client-sdk 5m
- owner: eng-console-sdk
- cardinality: medium (client_id, model_family)
- alert: critical if >0.25% sustained over 30m for high-traffic clients
- retention: raw examples logged for 7d in secure bucket (PII-scrubbed)

3) Latency-5th-to-95th-skew (tail skew index)
- calc: p95 latency / p50 latency per model-tenant-route 5m; track both token-gen and total-request
- owner: eng-sre-observability
- cardinality: per-tenant suggested (but rollup by weight)
- alert: warn if skew > 2.2 sustained 10m; critical if >3 AND p95 > target
- notes: split by cold-cache vs warm-cache using kvcache tag

4) Small-hallucination-index (syntactic mismatches)
- calc: proportion of outputs flagged by lightweight heuristic checks (e.g., unexpected URL patterns, off-domain entities) per eval-set-prompt cohorts
- owner: applied-ml
- cardinality: by model+prompt-cohort (low cardinality for cohorts)
- alert: increase in index by +25% vs baseline over 24h triggers investigation, use as guardrail not hard alert
- privacy: outputs hashed; raw snippets require PR review to view

5) Streaming-chunk-drop-rate
- calc: number of streaming partial-responses dropped / streaming sessions initiated
- owner: console-and-tooling
- cardinality: route, region
- alert: warn at 0.5% sustained 30m
- why: client-side UX regressions often show here early

6) Route-failover-latency-delta
- calc: latency difference between primary route and fallback in last 5m percentiles
- owner: platform-engineering
- cardinality: route pairs
- alert: if fallback > primary by 2x for p95 and traffic to primary decreases

7) Embedding-neighbor-entropy-drop
- calc: moving avg of top-10 neighbor cosine variance for embedding queries compared to baseline batch
- owner: product-hosted-api / applied-ml
- cardinality: dataset-cohort
- alert: incremental drop of >15% may indicate drift or encoding bug
- notes: expensive to compute; run on sample 0.05% QPS or daily snapshot

8) Unusual-configuration-surface
- calc: count of requests using experimental settings (e.g., custom-kv-ttl, prefill-buckets) not seen in last 7d
- owner: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services
- cardinality: high (config variant) but rollup by team
- alert: send to owners as informational, escalate if correlated with errors

Tracing and anchor strategy
- Span naming conventions (compact): service.operation:model_family:route (e.g., runtime.generate:gpt-j-16k:chat)
- Add trace tags for: tenant_id (hashed), request_route, model_version, kv_cache_hit (bool), cold_start_hint (bool), sample_bucket
- Anchor events: tokenized_input, kv_lookup_start, kv_lookup_end, kernel_launch, first_token_emitted, response_end
- Sampling: adaptive sampling. Always sample 100% of traces with error-status or eviction=true. For normal traffic sample 0.5% by default; bump to 5% for flagged tenants.
- Privacy: remove raw prompt and raw output from trace payloads in the public trace store; store hashes and truncated artifacts. Full examples go to secure logs with access control.

Operator workbench sketch (microcards)
- Top row: Global health: p50/p95 token latency, request success rate, token cost burn rate (1m window)
- Microcards (left column):
  * KV Warmth microcard: shows prefix-eviction-rate, kv-hit-rate, and median kv-lookup latency; clicking drills to recent traces with eviction=true
  * Tail skew microcard: p50/p95 with per-model toggles and quick filter to tenants with >X% weight
  * Streaming health: streaming-chunk-drop-rate and last 30 dropped traces thumbnails
- Right column: Quality signals: small-hallucination-index trend, embedding-entropy, recent eval regressions (linked)
- Bottom: Active anomalies queue (auto-populated): anomaly score, affected traffic %, top correlated signals, suggested runbook bullet (e.g., revert config, scale pool, disable rollout)

Drill path examples
- From KV Warmth microcard -> list of top 10 tenants with eviction events -> time series and 100 trace samples with eviction tag -> session reconstruction link -> reproduce prompt (sanitized) -> suggested action: increase kv TTL for route X or bump pool size

Alerting and thresholds guidance
- Keep primary alerts coarse and high-signal. Secondary early-warning alerts route to ops channel with playbook link and severity "investigate".
- Use composite alerts: e.g., high eviction AND p95>baseline*1.3 -> page oncall. Single-signal blips become CS/async tickets unless sustained.

Sampling and cost model (rough)
- Estimate: 1% trace sampling at 1200 QPS ~ 1.5 GB/day of trace storage. Preserve all eviction/error traces for 24h hot window then tier to cold store.
- For embedding entropy runs keep daily snapshot sampling (1k queries/day) per important cohort.

Open questions / discussion items
- How granular should tenant-level alerts be to avoid alert fatigue? Proposed: group low-traffic tenants into a "small-tenant" rollup by default.
- Small-hallucination-index: what lightweight heuristics do we accept as reliable enough to instrument widely? Need applied-ml input (Ravi).
- Retention policy: how long to keep eviction-tagged full traces in hot store? 24h vs 72h tradeoffs.

Immediate action items (next 3 sprints)
- Sprint 1: add kvcache eviction metric + tag traces with eviction=true (owner: serving-runtime). Instrumentation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/334 (Tomás)
- Sprint 2: implement microcard UI prototype for KV Warmth and Tail Skew (owner: observability-frontend, Lina)
- Sprint 3: light-weight hallucination heuristics prototype on eval prompts and low-traffic cohort (owner: applied-ml, Ravi)

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: favor signals that we can calculate from already emitted telemetry. If a metric requires heavy replay or new core runtime hooks, mark as medium-term.
- Please add realistic cost estimates for trace sampling changes and any privacy concerns for each signal.

Meeting notes snapshot (2026-02-14 sync)
- Agreement: prioritize kvcache eviction, tail-skew, streaming-drops for Q1.
- Action: Lina to spin up dashboard skeleton; Tomás to land eviction tag PR; Aisha to coordinate SLO-runbook tieins with SRE.

TODO (inline)

- [ ] Lina: mockup microcard interactions and provide widget size/cost guidance
